dense_lidar_stamp_origin.finding: The dense LiDAR replay node publishes Livox CustomMsg with reliable KeepLast(20); each timer tick assigns msg.header.stamp = now(), copies that stamp into livox_msg.header.stamp, and derives livox_msg.timebase from the header stamp.

imu_stamp_origin.finding: The IMU/state node publishes reliable KeepLast(64); each timer tick uses now() for IMU, TF, and truth odometry stamps. In 044 IMU remained monotonic.

fastlio_livox_callback_guard.finding: FAST-LIO livox_pcl_cbk computes cur_time from msg->header.stamp and clears the LiDAR buffer whenever cur_time < last_timestamp_lidar.

fastlio_subscription_qos.finding: FAST-LIO subscribes to Livox with depth 20 and IMU with depth 10. In 044 Livox publisher and FAST-LIO subscriber both used reliable queue depth 20.

topic_graph_findings.043_source_only_livox_subscriber_load: source recorder plus startup wait subscriber; no FAST-LIO subscriber

ruled_out: planner, RViz2, UE, TF bridge, PositionCommand, or 20Hz adapter involvement
supported: FAST-LIO presence changes early Livox subscriber load and queue topology.
The failing stream uses publisher-side node now() as the emitted header stamp rather than source-frame time.
The regression appears at the beginning of the 044 Livox stream while FAST-LIO has already accepted earlier LiDAR messages and last_timestamp_imu remains unset.
FAST-LIO's Livox callback reports the same early regressed message as a buffer-clearing loop-back.
not_proven: Whether the immediate trigger is node clock/wall-clock discontinuity, executor/timer startup ordering, DDS reliable queue behavior, discovery/startup wait subscriber interaction, or another subscriber-load effect.
Whether removing the wait-once subscriber, changing startup settle time, or adding publisher-side monotonic stamp instrumentation would eliminate the event.

next_minimal_diagnostic.scope: separately authorized evidence-local publisher-side timestamp instrumentation
details: Record for each dense LiDAR publish: frame index, source frame time, steady_clock timestamp, node now() before/after publish, emitted header stamp, timebase, publish duration, and current livox publisher matched-subscription count if available.
Keep one bounded FAST-LIO-only no-goal probe if PMO authorizes runtime; do not start RViz2, UE, planner/EGO, TF bridge, PositionCommand, or 20Hz adapter.
Do not change production source/config/extrinsics/frame adapters; use Results/tmp or evidence-local copy/instrumentation only.

disposable_subagent_audit.agreement: Subagent independently classified the likely mechanism as publisher timestamp source/load sensitivity at startup with secondary startup/subscriber-load boundary trigger.
key_notes: The observed Livox topic stream itself regressed in 044, so a purely FAST-LIO-local buffer explanation is insufficient.
FAST-LIO livox_pcl_cbk appears to react to the same non-monotonic Livox header stamp seen by the recorder.
DDS should normally preserve per-writer ordering, so publisher-side trace is needed before blaming DDS as sole cause.

claim_boundary: Static startup/DDS/subscriber-load diagnosis only; no new live ROS2 evidence and no FAST-LIO success, TF/RViz readiness, localization quality, local-map quality, planner_ready, controller performance, mission success, or closed_loop claim.
